::: {#exm-table-language}
#### What the table's DFA accepts

@fig-110 draws the DFA $W$ of @exr-table-trace.
Its language (@def-automaton-language) is the set of strings over $\set{\mathtt{0}, \mathtt{1}}$
that contain $\mathtt{110}$ as three symbols in a row.
Each state records how much of $\mathtt{110}$ the last symbols read have matched:

- $p_0$: none of it;
- $p_1$: the last symbol read is a $\mathtt{1}$ that follows no other $\mathtt{1}$, the start of $\mathtt{110}$;
- $p_2$: the last two symbols read are $\mathtt{11}$;
- $p_3$: $\mathtt{110}$ has appeared, and $p_3$ is accepting, with both of its arrows leading back to it.

A $\mathtt{0}$ read at $p_1$ goes back to $p_0$, since a string ending in $\mathtt{10}$ has matched none of $\mathtt{110}$,
while a $\mathtt{1}$ read at $p_2$ stays at $p_2$, since a string ending in $\mathtt{111}$ still ends in $\mathtt{11}$.
So $W$ accepts $\mathtt{0101100}$, as in @sol-table-trace, and rejects $\mathtt{101011}$, which does not contain $\mathtt{110}$.

::: {#fig-110}
